### Questionnaire (`questionnaire`)

Manga-styled wrapper around your shadcn Questionnaire (one question at a time, the kind an AI agent asks). The whole form is a case (3px ink line, tone shadow). Progress reads “Question 2 of 4” in lettering beside a 2px ink rail filled with speed lines that moves in steps. Each question pops in over three frames; titles are lettering, descriptions the reading face. Each choice is a choice card: a 2px ink frame whose line thickens on hover, with the ink / paper / ink focus ring around the row; checked, a 6px ink bar grows down its start edge and the indicator fills with ink (radio = a diamond with a paper dot, checkbox = a square with a brush check that draws itself). Shortcuts are key caps. The free-text input is the kit Input. Errors: accent line, a “!” mark and one shake. Previous / Skip are outline buttons, Next / Submit ink buttons, all with the impact on click. Disabled choices: dashed line and tone frame, label on paper.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/questionnaire`
- Categories: actions
- Props:
  - `shortcuts`: `"letters" | "numbers"` — On Questionnaire: shows a key cap on each choice and picks it on key press.
  - `multiple`: `boolean` (default `false`) — On QuestionnaireItem: square checkboxes instead of radio diamonds.
  - `required / invalid`: `boolean` — On QuestionnaireItem: required hides Skip; invalid shows the error look and QuestionnaireError.
  - `disabled / defaultChecked`: `boolean` — On QuestionnaireChoice: the dashed disabled card / a pre-checked choice.
  - `variant / size`: `shadcn Button variant / size` — On Previous, Skip, Next, Submit: drawn with the kit button look (outline for Previous / Skip, ink for Next / Submit by default).

```tsx
import {
  Questionnaire, QuestionnaireActions, QuestionnaireChoice, QuestionnaireChoices, QuestionnaireError,
  QuestionnaireItem, QuestionnaireNext, QuestionnairePrevious, QuestionnaireProgress, QuestionnaireSubmit, QuestionnaireTitle,
} from "@/components/ui/manga/questionnaire"

<Questionnaire shortcuts="letters" onSubmit={save}>
  <QuestionnaireProgress />
  <QuestionnaireItem name="genre" required>
    <QuestionnaireTitle>Which genre?</QuestionnaireTitle>
    <QuestionnaireChoices>
      <QuestionnaireChoice value="action">Action</QuestionnaireChoice>
      <QuestionnaireChoice value="romance">Romance</QuestionnaireChoice>
    </QuestionnaireChoices>
    <QuestionnaireError />
  </QuestionnaireItem>
  <QuestionnaireActions>
    <QuestionnairePrevious />
    <QuestionnaireNext />
    <QuestionnaireSubmit />
  </QuestionnaireActions>
</Questionnaire>
```

### Trace (`trace`)

Manga-styled wrapper around your shadcn Trace (the log of steps an agent ran). Every line is reading text in ink, never faded. An empty TraceIcon shows the mark of the line's status: done = a brush check, running = turning concentration lines (the kit Spinner, instead of the stock shimmer), pending = a small hollow square (no dashes: dashes mean disabled), error = accent text and a “!” mark. Lines inside a link or button are underlined; the underline thickens on hover and focus draws the ink / paper / ink ring. A collapsible group has a brush chevron that turns in two steps and content that unfolds in steps along a 1px ink rail on the start side. Durations (TraceDescription) are small mono, in ink.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/trace`
- Categories: feedback
- Props:
  - `status`: `"running" | "error" | "pending"` — On TraceLine. Omitted = done (brush check).
  - `TraceIcon children`: `ReactNode` — Optional. Your own icon, as in stock shadcn. Leave it out to get the automatic status mark (a mangacn addition): check, Spinner, hollow square or "!" from the line's status.
  - `TraceCollapsible`: `component` — A group of lines: TraceCollapsibleTrigger (wraps a TraceLine) and TraceCollapsibleContent.

```tsx
import { Trace, TraceDescription, TraceIcon, TraceLine, TraceTitle } from "@/components/ui/manga/trace"

<Trace>
  <TraceLine>
    <TraceIcon />
    <TraceTitle>Read chapter-12.md</TraceTitle>
    <TraceDescription>0.4s</TraceDescription>
  </TraceLine>
  <TraceLine status="running">
    <TraceIcon />
    <TraceTitle>Inking page 9…</TraceTitle>
  </TraceLine>
</Trace>
```

### Code Block (`code-block`)

Manga-styled wrapper around your shadcn Code Block: a 2px ink frame on paper, the file name in lettering above a fine rule, the code in mono, ink only (syntax colours are monochrome). Line numbers in ink. Line variants: highlighted (a 6px ink bar), added (bar and "+"), removed (accent bar, accent "−", struck text). Size sm, destructive frame. The copy button is an ink-framed square: hover thickens its line, focus draws the ink, click plays an impact, and the check icon shows once copied. Long lines scroll inside the block, never the page.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/code-block`
- Categories: display
- Props:
  - `variant`: `"default" | "destructive"` (default `"default"`) — On CodeBlock: destructive draws the frame and the text in the accent.
  - `size`: `"default" | "sm"` (default `"default"`) — On CodeBlock: smaller type and padding.
  - `lineNumbers / startLine`: `boolean / number` (default `false / 1`) — On CodeBlockContent: number the lines in ink, from startLine.
  - `wrap`: `boolean` (default `false`) — On CodeBlockContent: wrap long lines instead of scrolling them.
  - `variant`: `"default" | "highlighted" | "added" | "removed"` (default `"default"`) — On CodeBlockLine: the bar and mark of the line.
  - `value`: `string` — On CodeBlockCopyButton: the text copied to the clipboard.

```tsx
import { CodeBlock, CodeBlockHeader, CodeBlockTitle, CodeBlockActions, CodeBlockCopyButton, CodeBlockContent, CodeBlockLine } from "@/components/ui/manga/code-block"

<CodeBlock>
  <CodeBlockHeader>
    <CodeBlockTitle>hero.tsx</CodeBlockTitle>
    <CodeBlockActions><CodeBlockCopyButton value={code} /></CodeBlockActions>
  </CodeBlockHeader>
  <CodeBlockContent lineNumbers>
    <CodeBlockLine variant="added">{"return <Button />"}</CodeBlockLine>
  </CodeBlockContent>
</CodeBlock>
```

### Direction (`direction`)

Plain re-export of shadcn's Direction provider (DirectionProvider and useDirection), with the same API. Nothing is dressed: direction has no manga effect. It always takes `direction` ("ltr" or "rtl"), which both the Base UI and the Radix versions accept. The writing direction (dir) is what the kit's logical properties and rtl: variants follow; the manga reading order (data-reading) is a separate setting.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/direction`
- Categories: foundations
- Props:
  - `direction`: `"ltr" | "rtl"` — The direction the subtree is laid out in. Set dir on the element too, so CSS follows.
  - `useDirection()`: `hook` — Returns the current direction from the nearest provider.

```tsx
import { DirectionProvider, useDirection } from "@/components/ui/manga/direction"

<DirectionProvider direction="rtl">
  <div dir="rtl">...</div>
</DirectionProvider>
```

### Typing Bubble (`typing-bubble`)

A speech or thought bubble (the kit SpeechBubble) that first shows three small ink squares rising one after another at 12 fps (waiting), then writes its text a few characters per frame with a stepped block caret. The whole text is laid out from the start (the rest is invisible), so the bubble never reflows. Text that grows over time (streamed answers) types on from where it stopped, never from zero. The typed text is aria-hidden; a visually hidden copy is announced once, complete, through aria-live="polite"; the dots are role="status" with aria-label="Typing". Reduced motion: still dots, the text at once. Gestures: G6 bubble, G7 waiting.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/typing-bubble`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `text`: `string` — The text to write. It may grow over time: only the new characters animate.
  - `typing`: `boolean` (default `!text`) — Show the three waiting dots; the writing pauses meanwhile.
  - `speed`: `number` (default `3`) — Characters per frame at 12 fps. 0 shows the text at once.
  - `variant`: `"speech" | "thought"` (default `"speech"`) — Bubble shape.
  - `tail / tailAlign`: `SpeechBubble tail props` (default `"bottom" / "start"`) — Where the tail points, as in SpeechBubble.
  - `onDone`: `() => void` — Called each time the visible text catches up with text.
  - `progress`: `number` — Freezes the writing at this fraction (0–1), caret included: for previews and state grids.

```tsx
import { TypingBubble } from "@/components/manga/typing-bubble"

<TypingBubble text={answer} typing={!answer} onDone={() => setReady(true)} />
```

### Reaction Picker (`reaction-picker`)

A row of reactions drawn as manpu marks (anger, sweat, surprise, question, sparkle, gloom, love, sigh), each a toggle chip with its count in the SFX face: 2px ink frame, sharp corners. A chip is a button with aria-pressed; reacted = ink flat sweeping in (G2), hover thickens the line (G3, small cells), a click hits with speed lines (G4) and the count takes the hit when it changes; new chips pop in (G5). A "+" chip opens the kit Popover bubble (G6) with the eight marks as labelled buttons ("React with anger"); picking one toggles it and closes. Arrow keys move inside the grid. The row wraps; 44px targets under 640px. Controlled: pass reactions and toggle them in onReact. max caps the different kinds in the row; disabled makes it read-only (dashed chips). Exports ReactionChip and ReactionGrid for custom layouts and frozen previews.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/reaction-picker`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `reactions`: `{ kind: ManpuKind; count: number; active?: boolean }[]` — The row, in order. active = the reader reacted with it. Entries at 0 that are not active are hidden.
  - `onReact`: `(kind: ManpuKind) => void` — A chip or a mark of the picker was clicked: toggle that kind in your state.
  - `kinds`: `ManpuKind[]` (default `all eight`) — Marks offered in the picker.
  - `max`: `number` — The most different kinds the row holds; once full, the other marks of the picker are disabled.
  - `disabled`: `boolean` (default `false`) — Read-only row: dashed chips, no picker.

```tsx
import { ReactionPicker } from "@/components/manga/reaction-picker"

<ReactionPicker
  reactions={[{ kind: "love", count: 12, active: true }, { kind: "sweat", count: 2 }]}
  onReact={(kind) => toggle(kind)}
/>
```

### Reader Strip (`reader-strip`)

A vertical strip of page images for scroll (webtoon) reading, centred, full width on phones and at most 720px (or the widest page) on desktop. It follows the page scroll or the nearest scroll parent: no inner scroll box. Each page is a <figure> with a lazy <img> whose width and height reserve the space (no jump), framed by a 2px ink line unless gap is "none". Page states: loading = a paper panel of the page's ratio with a tone frame and the kit Spinner (G7); error = an accent edge-jagged panel with a "!" and a Retry button (G8) that asks the image again; loaded = the art pops in (G5). After the last page, an end panel (3px frame, SFX "END", brush mark-check, "To be continued"), announced to screen readers when reached. Reports progress (0-1 and the page in the middle of the view) with a requestAnimationFrame-throttled scroll listener, cleaned up on unmount. Exports ReaderStrip, ReaderPage (one page, with a status prop to freeze a state) and ReaderEnd (the end panel).

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/reader-strip`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `pages`: `{ src: string; alt: string; width: number; height: number }[]` — The page images, in reading order. width / height reserve the space.
  - `gap`: `"none" | "sm" | "md"` (default `"sm"`) — Space between pages; "none" joins them without frames.
  - `onProgress`: `(ratio: number, pageIndex: number) => void` — Scroll progress through the strip (0-1) and the page in the middle of the view (0-based).
  - `onEnd`: `() => void` — Called each time the end panel comes into view.
  - `onRetry`: `(pageIndex: number) => void` — Called when the reader retries a failed page (e.g. to switch source).
  - `end`: `ReactNode` (default `<ReaderEnd />`) — Shown after the last page.
  - `aria-label`: `string` (default `"Pages"`) — Name of the strip (a <section>).

```tsx
import { ReaderStrip } from "@/components/manga/reader-strip"

<ReaderStrip
  aria-label="Chapter 12"
  pages={[{ src: "/ch12/01.webp", alt: "The city at night", width: 800, height: 1200 }]}
  onProgress={(ratio, page) => setPage(page + 1)}
  onEnd={() => markRead()}
/>
```

### Reading Progress (`reading-progress`)

A reading progress bar: a 2px ink baseline with an ink fill-lines bar sitting on it (G7), in whole pixels; the bar shares the baseline's outer edge and grows inward, 4px of solid ink at rest and 6px with a paper speed line through it while the reader scrolls or the value changes. Measures the scroll of a target element (its own scroll, or how far the window has moved through it) or of the window, with requestAnimationFrame, cleaned up on unmount; or takes a controlled value (then the width moves in steps). Positions: fixed to the top or bottom edge of the viewport, or inline in the flow. In manga reading order (data-reading="rtl") it fills from the right. Optional value text ("42 %" or "Page 3 / 8") on paper, never on the lines. role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max and aria-valuetext. Reduced motion: no motion, the value still updates. Also exports useScrollProgress(target).

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/reading-progress`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `value`: `number` — 0-100, controlled. Leave out to measure the scroll.
  - `target`: `RefObject<HTMLElement | null>` — Element whose scroll progress is measured. Default: the window.
  - `position`: `"top" | "bottom" | "inline"` (default `"inline"`) — Fixed to that edge of the viewport, or in the flow.
  - `label`: `string` (default `"Reading progress"`) — Accessible name.
  - `showValue`: `boolean` (default `false`) — Shows the value as a small text.
  - `valueText`: `string` (default `"42 %"`) — Text for the value, e.g. "Page 3 / 8"; also aria-valuetext.

```tsx
import { ReadingProgress } from "@/components/manga/reading-progress"

<ReadingProgress position="top" />
<ReadingProgress value={37.5} showValue valueText="Page 3 / 8" />
```

### Page Reader (`page-reader`)

A manga read page by page from a list of images ({ src, alt, width, height }). One page or two-page spreads (auto: spreads when the stage is wide and landscape; the cover stands alone), manga order (right to left: the next page is on the left, a spread puts the lower page on the right) or western order. Turn with the page edges (invisible zones that show a paper plate with a brush arrow on hover), the arrow keys (following the order), Page Up / Down, Home / End, a swipe (the page follows the finger with no steps, then turns or snaps back; it resists at both ends) or the toolbar. Fit: whole page, width (scrolls down) or height. Background: paper, ink or tone. Zoom 100–300 % with buttons, + / - / 0 or a double click at a point, then drag to pan. Full screen asks the browser (Fullscreen API on the document) and falls back to a fixed immersive mode (iOS Safari); Escape leaves. Pages around the current one are fetched ahead (preload), and a page known to be loaded shows at once. Each page is a ReaderPage (ink frame, loading panel, jagged error panel with Retry, a paper mat in dark mode). A turned page slides in from the side it comes from in three steps. An optional end view after the last page holds a ChapterEnd. The toolbar has a ReadingProgress with a page counter and a slot for your own buttons (settings, thumbnails). Controlled or not (page / onPageChange). Built at 375 px first: 44 px controls, two toolbar rows. PageReader also takes pages of the page model ({ page: PageData }), drawn by Page with real lettering; scans and data pages can be mixed.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/page-reader`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `pages`: `({ src: string; alt: string; width: number; height: number } | { page: PageData; alt?: string })[]` — Scans, or pages of the page model, in reading order.
  - `page`: `number` — First page shown (0-based), controlled. pages.length is the end view when end is set.
  - `defaultPage`: `number` (default `0`) — First page shown, uncontrolled.
  - `onPageChange`: `(page: number) => void` — Called with the first page of the new view.
  - `spread`: `"single" | "double" | "auto"` (default `"auto"`) — One page, two-page spreads, or spreads when the stage is wide and landscape.
  - `coverAlone`: `boolean` (default `true`) — In spreads, the first page stands alone.
  - `direction`: `"rtl" | "ltr"` (default `"rtl"`) — Manga order (next page on the left) or western order.
  - `fit`: `"contain" | "width" | "height"` (default `"contain"`) — Whole page in view, fill the width (scrolls down) or fill the height.
  - `background`: `"paper" | "ink" | "tone"` (default `"paper"`) — What shows around the pages. "ink" stays black in both themes.
  - `preload`: `number` (default `2`) — Pages fetched ahead of and behind the view.
  - `end`: `ReactNode` — One more view after the last page, e.g. a ChapterEnd.
  - `onEnd`: `() => void` — Called on reaching the end view, or on asking past the last page when there is none.
  - `toolbar`: `ReactNode` — Your own buttons in the toolbar (settings, thumbnails).
  - `className`: `string` — Added to the root; set its height here (default min(48rem, 88svh)).

```tsx
import { PageReader } from "@/components/manga/page-reader"
import { ChapterEnd } from "@/components/manga/chapter-end"

<PageReader
  pages={pages}
  direction="rtl"
  spread="auto"
  onPageChange={(page) => save(page)}
  end={<ChapterEnd chapter="Chapter 4" next={{ number: 5, title: "Paper boats", href: "/read/5" }} />}
/>
```

### Page Thumbnails (`page-thumbnails`)

Every page of a chapter in a grid, to jump anywhere: a nav of numbered page buttons, each a small 2px case with the page (lazy image, aspect from its width and height, a paper mat in dark mode so scans stay light) and its number on a fine plate. The page on screen (one, or two for a spread) has a 3px frame and its number plate is an ink flat that sweeps in (aria-current=page); pages already read carry a brush check. Hover lift, ink focus ring, pressed offset. In manga order the grid runs right to left. The columns fill the width from a minimum size (three at 375 px). When it opens inside a dialog or a scroll frame, the page being read is scrolled into view. It also takes pages of the page model ({ page: PageData }), drawn small by Page.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/page-thumbnails`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `pages`: `({ src: string; alt: string; width: number; height: number } | { page: PageData; alt?: string })[]` — Scans, or pages of the page model, in reading order.
  - `current`: `number | number[]` — The page or pages on screen.
  - `readUntil`: `number` (default `0`) — Pages before this index get a brush check.
  - `onSelect`: `(page: number) => void` — Called with the page chosen.
  - `direction`: `"rtl" | "ltr"` (default `"rtl"`) — The grid runs right to left (manga) or left to right.
  - `minWidth`: `string` (default `"5.5rem"`) — Smallest thumbnail width (CSS length).
  - `className`: `string` — Added to the nav.

```tsx
import { PageThumbnails } from "@/components/manga/page-thumbnails"

<PageThumbnails
  pages={pages}
  current={page}
  readUntil={page}
  direction="rtl"
  onSelect={(i) => setPage(i)}
/>
```

### Guided View (`guided-view`)

A manga read panel by panel, made for phones: the screen zooms from one panel to the next. It reads the panel geometry of the page model (pageGeometry: every panel's box in reading order, insets included), so a page written as PageData is drawn by Page and guided without any extra data; scans work too, with the box of each panel in percent of the page. The page is drawn once at a fixed width and a camera fits the current panel in the stage, moving in four steps (333 ms); the panels around it hide under a paper veil with wide dots that steps aside while the camera travels. A new page slides in from the side it comes from. Next and previous by tapping the page edges (on hover a paper plate with a brush arrow), the arrow keys following the reading order, Space, Page Up / Down, Home / End, a swipe (the page follows the finger, then turns or snaps back) or the toolbar. Whole page shows the page with every panel as a target (the current one framed, hover thickens a panel's line). A ReadingProgress counts the panels; a live region reads each panel's label. Optional end view (e.g. a ChapterEnd) and a slot for your buttons. Reduced motion: the camera jumps.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/guided-view`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `pages`: `({ page: PageData; alt?: string } | { src: string; alt: string; width: number; height: number; panels: { x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number; label?: string }[] })[]` — Page-model pages, or scans with their panel boxes (percent of the page).
  - `position`: `{ page: number; panel: number }` — Current panel, controlled (0-based).
  - `defaultPosition`: `{ page: number; panel: number }` (default `{ page: 0, panel: 0 }`) — Current panel, uncontrolled.
  - `onPositionChange`: `(position: { page: number; panel: number }) => void` — Called at each step.
  - `direction`: `"rtl" | "ltr"` (default `"rtl"`) — Order of taps, swipes and arrows, and of data pages that do not set reading.
  - `end`: `ReactNode` — Shown after the last panel.
  - `onEnd`: `() => void` — Called past the last panel.
  - `toolbar`: `ReactNode` — Your own buttons in the toolbar.
  - `className`: `string` — Added to the root; set its height here (default min(46rem, 86svh)).

```tsx
import { GuidedView } from "@/components/manga/guided-view"
import type { PageData } from "@/components/manga/page-geometry"

const pages: PageData[] = [/* your pages */]

<GuidedView
  pages={pages.map((page) => ({ page }))}
  direction="rtl"
  onPositionChange={({ page, panel }) => save(page, panel)}
/>
```

### Reader Settings (`reader-settings`)

Settings for a manga reader: reading order (manga right to left, western left to right), mode (page, double page, strip), fit (whole page, width, height) and background (paper, ink, tone). Each setting is a radio group drawn like boxed tabs: one 2px frame split into cells of at least 44 px, each with a small drawn pictogram and a lettering label; the chosen cell is an ink flat that sweeps in, hover thickens the line, focus stays inside the cell (a paper line on the chosen ink cell), pressed moves 1px. Arrows move and choose (following the writing direction), Home / End, Tab leaves. A setting can be hidden or shown disabled (dashed frame, tone frame in the cells, the chosen label underlined on paper). Controlled or not; it only holds the value: put it in a Sheet, a Popover or a page and feed PageReader.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/reader-settings`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `value`: `{ direction: "rtl" | "ltr"; mode: "single" | "double" | "strip"; fit: "contain" | "width" | "height"; background: "paper" | "ink" | "tone" }` — The settings, controlled.
  - `defaultValue`: `ReaderSettingsValue` (default `defaultReaderSettings`) — Manga order, single page, whole page, paper.
  - `onValueChange`: `(value: ReaderSettingsValue) => void` — Called with the whole new value.
  - `hide`: `("direction" | "mode" | "fit" | "background")[]` — Settings left out.
  - `disabled`: `("direction" | "mode" | "fit" | "background")[]` — Settings shown but not changeable.
  - `className`: `string` — Added to the root.

```tsx
import { ReaderSettings, defaultReaderSettings } from "@/components/manga/reader-settings"

const [settings, setSettings] = React.useState(defaultReaderSettings)

<ReaderSettings value={settings} onValueChange={setSettings} />
```

### Chapter End (`chapter-end`)

The end card of a chapter: a 3px panel whose concentration lines surround a central paper plate, with the chapter line, the big SFX word (To be continued, or The end for a finished series) and a brush arrow in the reading direction (a check at the end of a series). Under it, the next chapter as a full-width button with its number, title and optional cover, or, when it is not out yet, the date in a stamp; then any actions the reader wants (back to the series, comments). Under the manga reading order (data-reading="rtl") the arrow points left. The panel pops in once.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/chapter-end`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `chapter`: `ReactNode` — The chapter just read, shown as "End of {chapter}".
  - `variant`: `"continued" | "end"` (default `"continued"`) — continued: more to come (arrow) · end: the series is over (check).
  - `title`: `string` (default `"To be continued" or "The end"`) — The big SFX word.
  - `next`: `{ number, title, href?, onSelect?, cover?, date? }` — The next chapter. Without href or onSelect it is not out yet and shows "Out on {date}".
  - `children`: `ReactNode` — Extra actions, in a wrapping row under the next chapter.
  - `className`: `string` — Added to the panel.

```tsx
import { ChapterEnd } from "@/components/manga/chapter-end"

<ChapterEnd
  chapter="Chapter 12 · Echo"
  next={{ number: 13, title: "Quiet Engine", href: "/read/13", cover: "/covers/13.jpg" }}
>
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Back to series</Button>
</ChapterEnd>
```

### Shelf (`shelf`)

Manga volumes standing spine out on a shelf. Each spine is a 2px case at least 44 px wide (three thicknesses, slightly varied heights) with the volume number on an ink flat at the top, the title in vertical lettering and an optional tone band or tone ends (never under text); the plank is a 3px ink edge, a band of tone lines and another edge. Hover lifts the spine's tone shadow, focus is the ink ring, pressed the 2px offset. Pulling a volume (click, Enter) turns its spine into an ink flat raised by 16px in two steps and drops its VolumeCard in under the shelf (cover, status, reading progress) with Open and Put back buttons. Arrows move along the row, Home / End, Escape puts the volume back and returns the focus to its spine. The row scrolls sideways when it is wider than the screen; in manga order volume 1 stands at the right end. Controlled or not (selected / onSelectedChange).

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/shelf`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `volumes`: `ShelfVolume[]` — { id, title, volume, author?, cover?, status?, read?, total?, thickness?: 1 | 2 | 3, spine?: "plain" | "band" | "tone" }.
  - `selected`: `string | null` — Id of the pulled volume, controlled.
  - `defaultSelected`: `string | null` (default `null`) — Pulled volume, uncontrolled.
  - `onSelectedChange`: `(id: string | null) => void` — Called when a volume is pulled or put back.
  - `onOpen`: `(volume: ShelfVolume) => void` — Called by the Open button of the pulled volume.
  - `openLabel`: `string` (default `"Open"`) — Label of that button.
  - `direction`: `"ltr" | "rtl"` (default `"ltr"`) — Volume 1 at the left, or at the right (manga order).
  - `className`: `string` — Added to the root.

```tsx
import { Shelf } from "@/components/manga/shelf"

<Shelf
  volumes={[
    { id: "ls-1", title: "Lantern Street", volume: 1, cover: "/covers/ls-1.jpg", status: "completed", read: 8, total: 8 },
    { id: "ls-2", title: "Lantern Street", volume: 2, cover: "/covers/ls-2.jpg", status: "ongoing", read: 3, total: 8, spine: "band" },
  ]}
  openLabel="Read"
  onOpen={(v) => router.push(`/read/${v.id}`)}
/>
```

### Series Header (`series-header`)

The head of a manga series page, in a case: a 2:3 cover in a 2px case (image URL or any node; a screentone without one), the status as a Stamp (accent for new, ink for ongoing, completed and hiatus), the title in big lettering, an alternative title, the author, genres as outline Badges, up to four figures (chapters, volumes, readers) in a frame split into cells, a summary folded to a few lines with a Read more / Show less link (shown only when the text is cut; the unfolded text drops in) and your actions. At 375 px the cover sits beside the title and the rest takes the full width; in a wide container everything but the cover forms one column beside it (container queries, so it adapts to its column, not the window).

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/series-header`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `title`: `ReactNode` — Set in big lettering.
  - `cover`: `string | ReactNode` — Image URL or any node, in a 2:3 box. Without it, a screentone.
  - `altTitle`: `ReactNode` — Original or alternative title.
  - `author`: `ReactNode` — Author line.
  - `status`: `"new" | "ongoing" | "completed" | "hiatus"` — Shown as a stamp.
  - `genres`: `string[]` — Shown as outline badges.
  - `stats`: `{ label: ReactNode; value: ReactNode }[]` — Up to four figures.
  - `summary`: `ReactNode` — Folded to summaryLines lines with Read more.
  - `summaryLines`: `2 | 3 | 4 | 5` (default `3`) — Lines shown while folded.
  - `actions`: `ReactNode` — Buttons or links.
  - `as`: `"h1" | "h2" | "h3"` (default `"h1"`) — Heading level of the title.
  - `className`: `string` — Added to the case.

```tsx
import { SeriesHeader } from "@/components/manga/series-header"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/manga/button"

<SeriesHeader
  title="Lantern Street"
  author="N. Arai"
  cover="/covers/lantern-street.jpg"
  status="ongoing"
  genres={["Slice of life", "Mystery"]}
  stats={[{ label: "Chapters", value: 38 }, { label: "Volumes", value: 4 }]}
  summary="Every autumn the night market…"
  actions={<><Button>Start reading</Button><Button variant="outline">Add to shelf</Button></>}
/>
```

### Obi Band (`obi-band`)

The paper promotional band wrapped round the lower part of a manga volume. It takes a 2:3 cover (an image URL, or any node) and overhangs it by a few pixels at the bottom, with a 2px ink line on each side and a fold strip at the start edge. Tones: accent (the kit's one colour), ink (an ink flat) or paper (a screentone strip on the top edge only). Sizes sm, md, lg set the band height (26, 34, 42 % of the cover). The headline scales with the cover width through container queries, so it works on a 120 px cover too. An optional badge is a burst at the band's end corner. Static, not interactive.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/obi-band`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `cover`: `string | ReactNode` — An image URL (object-cover), or any node drawn as the cover. Takes precedence over children.
  - `children`: `ReactNode` — Drawn in the 2:3 box when no cover is given.
  - `headline`: `ReactNode` — The big catchphrase, in lettering.
  - `caption`: `ReactNode` — A small line under the headline.
  - `badge`: `ReactNode` — A short word in a burst at the band's end corner, e.g. "NEW".
  - `tone`: `"accent" | "ink" | "paper"` (default `"accent"`) — accent: the kit's accent · ink: an ink flat · paper: paper with a screentone top edge.
  - `size`: `"sm" | "md" | "lg"` (default `"md"`) — Band height: 26 %, 34 % or 42 % of the cover.
  - `className`: `string` — Added to the root.

```tsx
import { ObiBand } from "@/components/manga/obi-band"

<ObiBand
  cover="/covers/night-rail-2.jpg"
  headline="Over 2 million copies"
  caption="Now a major series"
  badge="NEW"
  tone="accent"
  size="md"
/>
```

### Spoiler (`spoiler`)

Content hidden by a screentone, revealed on click. Block: the children stay in the layout but are inert and aria-hidden under a tone cover with a paper plate that names what is hidden ("Chapter 12 ending") and says "Tap to reveal"; the plate gets a tone shadow on hover, the cover has the ink focus ring and a pressed offset, and the content pops in on reveal with a Hide button to cover it again. Inline: a few words become an ink flat with transparent text, a paper inner line on hover, and the revealed words get a 2px underline. Controlled (revealed, onRevealedChange) or uncontrolled (defaultRevealed).

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/spoiler`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `variant`: `"block" | "inline"` (default `"block"`) — block: an image or a paragraph under a cover · inline: a few words in a sentence.
  - `label`: `string` (default `"Spoiler"`) — What it hides, read in the reveal button's name and shown on the plate (block).
  - `revealed`: `boolean` — Controlled reveal state.
  - `defaultRevealed`: `boolean` (default `false`) — Initial reveal state when uncontrolled.
  - `onRevealedChange`: `(revealed: boolean) => void` — Called when the reader reveals or hides it.
  - `triggerProps`: `ButtonHTMLAttributes & data-*` — Extra attributes for the reveal button (showcase states).
  - `className`: `string` — Added to the root (block) or to the reveal button / revealed text (inline).

```tsx
import { Spoiler } from "@/components/manga/spoiler"

<Spoiler label="Chapter 12 ending">
  <img src="/panels/ch12-last.jpg" alt="The final panel of chapter 12" />
</Spoiler>

<p>
  The letter was signed by <Spoiler variant="inline" label="the editor">the editor</Spoiler>.
</p>
```

### Ranking List (`ranking-list`)

A ranking with big numbers in a case: the rank in the SFX face (the top ranks biggest, the first place in the accent), an optional 2:3 cover thumbnail in a 2px ink frame, the title in lettering and a subtitle, an optional score, and the change at the end: an up or down brush arrow with its count, an en dash for no change, or a NEW burst. Rows are separated by 2px ink lines. Rows with href are links, rows with onSelect are buttons: both invert to ink on hover, and press to a paper negative with a 2px offset. Logical properties only, so dir=rtl works.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/ranking-list`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `entries`: `RankingEntry[]` — Rows: id, title, subtitle, cover, change (number or "new"), score, href.
  - `onSelect`: `(entry: RankingEntry, index: number) => void` — Makes the rows without href buttons.
  - `start`: `number` (default `1`) — First rank shown.
  - `highlightTop`: `number` (default `3`) — Ranks up to this one get the biggest numbers. Rank 1 is in the accent.
  - `className`: `string` — Added to the list.

```tsx
import { RankingList, type RankingEntry } from "@/components/manga/ranking-list"

const entries: RankingEntry[] = [
  { id: "glass-harbour", title: "Glass Harbour", subtitle: "M. Sato", change: 0, score: "1.2M", href: "/series/glass-harbour" },
  { id: "iron-lullaby", title: "Iron Lullaby", subtitle: "K. Hadley", change: 3, cover: "/covers/iron-lullaby.jpg", href: "/series/iron-lullaby" },
]

<RankingList entries={entries} />
```

### Release Calendar (`release-calendar`)

Releases by day of the week. On a narrow screen a day strip drawn like boxed tabs (one frame split into seven cells, the selected day an ink flat, today marked with a corner triangle) shows the releases of one day below it, with arrow, Home and End keys. From a container of 56 rem up, seven columns show every day at once, today's header an ink flat. Each release is a case with its cover, time, title and chapter, a NEW burst or a Break stamp; rows with an href are links, rows with onSelect are buttons, both with the hover lift, the ink focus ring and the pressed offset. A day without releases shows a short line in a fine frame.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/release-calendar`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `releases`: `Release[]` — Each release: id, day (0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday), title, optional chapter, time, cover (URL or node), status ("new" | "break") and href (makes the row a link).
  - `today`: `Weekday` (default `computed from the date`) — The day marked with the corner triangle and the ink header.
  - `day`: `Weekday` — Controlled day shown on narrow screens.
  - `defaultDay`: `Weekday` (default `today`) — Day shown first on narrow screens.
  - `onDayChange`: `(day: Weekday) => void` — Called when a day is picked in the strip.
  - `dayLabels`: `[string × 7]` (default `["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]`) — Short day labels, Monday first.
  - `onSelect`: `(release: Release) => void` — Makes the rows without an href buttons.
  - `empty`: `ReactNode` (default `"Nothing this day."`) — Shown on a day without releases.
  - `layout`: `"auto" | "strip" | "columns"` (default `"auto"`) — auto switches by the container width (56 rem); strip and columns force one layout.
  - `className`: `string` — Added to the root.

```tsx
import { ReleaseCalendar, type Release } from "@/components/manga/release-calendar"

const releases: Release[] = [
  { id: "1", day: 0, title: "Glass Harbor", chapter: "Ch. 1 · Low Tide", time: "06:00", status: "new", href: "/series/glass-harbor/1" },
  { id: "2", day: 2, title: "Paper Comet", chapter: "Ch. 18", time: "18:00", status: "break" },
]

<ReleaseCalendar releases={releases} today={2} onSelect={(r) => openRelease(r.id)} />
```

### Social Button (`social-button`)

"Continue with <service>" button for third-party sign-in. An outline button (2px ink line, lettering label, hover, pressed, focus, loading and disabled exactly like the manga Button), 44px tall and full width by default. A logo slot at the start: a bare 32 × 32 box that fits the given mark without recolouring, framing or redrawing it (a mark that needs a plate, like Google's icon on white, brings its own); the item ships no logo and no brand colour. AuthDivider is a horizontal fine ink rule with "or" in lettering in the middle. All Button props pass through; provider sets data-provider.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/social-button`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `logo`: `React.ReactNode` (default `undefined`) — The brand mark, used as its brand provides it (with its own plate when the brand asks for one), fitted into a bare 32 × 32 box. Omit it for a button without a logo.
  - `provider`: `string` (default `undefined`) — Sets data-provider on the button (e.g. "google", "apple").
  - `variant`: `"default" | "outline" | "tone" | "ghost" | "link" | "destructive" | "shout"` (default `"outline"`) — Inherited from the manga Button.
  - `fullWidth`: `boolean` (default `true`) — Stretches the button to the container width.
  - `loading`: `boolean` (default `false`) — Inherited from the manga Button: turning lines, aria-busy, clicks ignored.
  - `label (AuthDivider)`: `string` (default `"or"`) — Text in the middle of the divider; also its accessible label.

```tsx
import { SocialButton, AuthDivider } from "@/components/manga/social-button"

<SocialButton provider="google" logo={<GoogleMark />}>Continue with Google</SocialButton>
<AuthDivider />
<SocialButton provider="apple" logo={<AppleMark />} loading>Continue with Apple</SocialButton>
```

### Password Strength (`password-strength`)

A gauge under a password field: four segments (2px ink frame) that fill with speed lines, one after the other in steps; the top level is an ink flat. The label sits beside the gauge on paper and is announced politely; the gauge is role=meter. Props: value (the password, scored locally by passwordScore: length, lower/upper case, digits, symbols; no dictionary, no network) or score 0-4 (overrides value), labels (five, default Too short, Weak, Fair, Good, Strong), minLength (default 8). Also exports passwordScore(password, minLength?).

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/password-strength`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `value`: `string` (default `""`) — The password to estimate locally. Ignored when score is given.
  - `score`: `0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4` (default `undefined`) — A score from your own estimate. Overrides value.
  - `labels`: `string[]` (default `["Too short", "Weak", "Fair", "Good", "Strong"]`) — Five labels for the scores 0 to 4.
  - `minLength`: `number` (default `8`) — Passwords shorter than this score 0.

```tsx
import { PasswordStrength, passwordScore } from "@/components/manga/password-strength"

<Input type="password" value={pw} onChange={(e) => setPw(e.target.value)} />
<PasswordStrength value={pw} />
<PasswordStrength score={3} labels={["Empty", "Poor", "OK", "Good", "Great"]} />
```

### Yonkoma (`yonkoma`)

A four-panel strip read top to bottom, to explain something in four beats, built on the page model: a free-height Page (format strip) with one Tier per panel, or one Tier of four panels in a row in the manga reading order. The API is four children, one per panel, plus an optional title box; each panel is a named group for screen readers with a small number box in its corner. A child given as a fragment is spread into its panel, so Place elements in it (bubbles with pointAt, captions, Sfx) sit on the page and may cross the frame. The strip measures itself: frames stay about 3px and the lettering stays readable at any width. orientation="horizontal" puts the four in a row; "auto" stacks them, then lines them up once the strip is 40rem wide. Any aspect ratio per panel.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/yonkoma`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `children`: `ReactNode` — Four children, one per panel. Extra ones are left out.
  - `title`: `ReactNode` — Title box above the strip.
  - `numbered`: `boolean` (default `true`) — Number box in each panel's corner.
  - `labels`: `[string, string, string, string]` — Spoken description of each panel (default "Panel 1 of 4"…).
  - `orientation`: `"vertical" | "horizontal" | "auto"` (default `"vertical"`) — A column, a row in the reading order, or a column that becomes a row from 40rem.
  - `aspect`: `number | string` (default `"4 / 3"`) — Width / height of each panel, as a number or a CSS ratio.

```tsx
import { Place } from "@/components/manga/panel"
import { SpeechBubble } from "@/components/manga/speech-bubble"
import { Yonkoma } from "@/components/manga/yonkoma"

<Yonkoma title="How it works" labels={["Install", "Import", "Style", "Ship"]}>
  <StepOne />
  <StepTwo />
  <StepThree />
  <>
    <StepFour />
    <Place x={70} y={10}>
      <SpeechBubble pointAt={{ x: "50%", y: "70%" }}>Shipped!</SpeechBubble>
    </Place>
  </>
</Yonkoma>
```

### Dialogue Box (`dialogue-box`)

A character dialogue box for a queue of lines: a case with a square portrait (a case inside it) on the start or end side, the speaker on an ink name plate on the top edge (it pops when the speaker changes), the line writing itself at 12 fps with a stepped block caret and no reflow, and a 44px arrow button that shows the whole line at once while it writes, then goes to the next line (the arrow blinks in two hard steps), with a 2 / 5 count. A click on the text does the same. After the last line it loops or stays (loop={false}) and calls onEnd. Controlled or not; progress freezes a line for previews. Each finished line is announced; reduced motion shows lines at once.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/dialogue-box`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `lines`: `{ speaker; text: string; portrait?; side?: "start" | "end" }[]` — The queue of lines.
  - `index`: `number` — Current line (controlled).
  - `defaultIndex`: `number` (default `0`) — First line (uncontrolled).
  - `onIndexChange`: `(index: number) => void` — Called when the line changes.
  - `onEnd`: `() => void` — Called when the reader goes on after the last line.
  - `loop`: `boolean` (default `true`) — Start again after the last line; false stays on it.
  - `speed`: `number` (default `2`) — Characters per frame at 12 fps. 0 shows lines at once.
  - `progress`: `number` — Freezes the line at this fraction (0–1), for previews.
  - `showCount`: `boolean` (default `true`) — Shows "2 / 5" next to the arrow.
  - `labels`: `{ skip?; next?; end? }` — Spoken names of the arrow button in each state.

```tsx
import { DialogueBox } from "@/components/manga/dialogue-box"

<DialogueBox
  lines={[
    { speaker: "Sensei", portrait: "/faces/sensei.png", text: "Welcome to the studio." },
    { speaker: "Rookie", portrait: "/faces/rookie.png", side: "end", text: "Where do I start?" },
  ]}
  onEnd={() => setTutorialDone(true)}
/>
```

### Chapter Title (`chapter-title`)

A chapter title page used as a section header: a big number in the SFX face with a small label above it, the title in lettering (a real heading, read as "Chapter 3: title"), a 3px ink rule and an optional subtitle, and an optional column of vertical text at the end side against a narrow band of speed lines on its edge (never under the letters). Paper or ink. animated: the number pops and the rule grows from the start in steps when it appears; still with reduced motion.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/chapter-title`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `number`: `ReactNode` — The chapter number, shown big.
  - `title`: `ReactNode` — The heading.
  - `label`: `ReactNode` (default `"Chapter"`) — Small lettering above the number.
  - `subtitle`: `ReactNode` — A line under the rule.
  - `vertical`: `ReactNode` — A short column of vertical text at the end side.
  - `verticalLang`: `string` (default `"ja"`) — Language of the vertical text.
  - `as`: `"h1" | "h2" | "h3"` (default `"h2"`) — Heading level.
  - `titleId`: `string` — id of the heading.
  - `variant`: `"paper" | "ink"` (default `"paper"`) — Paper page or ink page.
  - `animated`: `boolean` (default `false`) — Number pops, rule grows when it appears.

```tsx
import { ChapterTitle } from "@/components/manga/chapter-title"

<section aria-labelledby="ch3">
  <ChapterTitle titleId="ch3" number="03" title="The first panel" vertical="第三話" />
  …
</section>
```

### Magazine Cover (`magazine-cover`)

A manga magazine cover in a 3:4 case: the masthead in the SFX face across a band of ink at the top with an optional tagline, the issue and date in a box at its end, cover lines on paper plates down both sides of the art (one may be an accent flat for the big news) and a headline plate at the foot. Every word rests on a flat, never on the art. The lettering scales with the cover (container units), from a thumbnail to full width on a phone. Static, a link (href) or a button (onSelect) with the hover lift, ink focus ring and pressed offset.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/magazine-cover`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `title`: `ReactNode` — The masthead.
  - `issue`: `ReactNode` — Issue number, in the box at the band's end.
  - `date`: `ReactNode` — Date or season under the issue.
  - `tagline`: `ReactNode` — A short line under the masthead.
  - `image`: `string | ReactNode` — Image URL or any node, filling the cover. Without it, a screentone.
  - `imageAlt`: `string` (default `""`) — Alternative text of an image URL.
  - `lines`: `{ text; side?: "start" | "end"; highlight? }[]` — Cover lines on plates around the art. highlight: an accent flat.
  - `headline`: `ReactNode` — The main cover line, on a plate at the foot.
  - `href`: `string` — Makes the cover a link.
  - `onSelect`: `() => void` — Makes the cover a button.

```tsx
import { MagazineCover } from "@/components/manga/magazine-cover"

<MagazineCover
  title="Weekly Ink"
  issue="No. 12"
  date="Spring"
  image="/covers/12.jpg"
  imageAlt="A rookie in front of a huge sun"
  lines={[{ text: "New series!", highlight: true }, { text: "Bonus poster", side: "end" }]}
  headline="The rookie's first page"
/>
```

### Scene Transition (`scene-transition`)

A wipe that sweeps the screen (or a container) between two sections or pages, in steps: four frames to cover, a hold, four frames to uncover, at 12 fps, swapping the scene while the screen is covered. Across in the reading order (right to left with data-reading="rtl" or dir="rtl") or downward. Variants: ink (an ink flat), tone (a 50% screentone on paper edged with ink lines), panels (four ink panels with paper gutters dropped one per frame). An optional caption pops in the middle during the hold, on a paper narration box. As a hook (useSceneTransition: play(swap) returns a promise) or a component (playing, onCovered, onDone). The overlay is aria-hidden and catches clicks while it plays; with reduced motion the scene is swapped at once.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/scene-transition`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `variant`: `"ink" | "tone" | "panels"` (default `"ink"`) — Ink flat, 50% screentone, or four ink panels.
  - `direction`: `"reading" | "down"` (default `"reading"`) — Across in the reading order, or from top to bottom.
  - `scope`: `"screen" | "container"` (default `"screen"`) — Fixed over the viewport, or over the nearest positioned ancestor.
  - `hold`: `number` (default `2`) — Frames the screen stays covered.
  - `caption`: `ReactNode` — Narration box shown in the middle while covered.
  - `playing`: `boolean` — Component only: plays each time it turns true.
  - `onCovered / onDone`: `() => void` — Component only: swap the scene / the scene is uncovered.
  - `frame`: `number` — Component only: freezes one frame, for previews.

```tsx
import { useSceneTransition } from "@/components/manga/scene-transition"

const { play, transition } = useSceneTransition({ variant: "panels", caption: "Meanwhile…" })

<button onClick={() => play(() => setPage(2))}>Next page</button>
{transition}
```

### Ruby (`ruby`)

Furigana: small readings over (or under, or beside in vertical text) the characters they read, in native <ruby> / <rt> markup with <rp> fallbacks so the text copies, wraps and reads aloud. One reading over a whole word (base + reading) or one per character (parts). reveal="hover" hides the readings for learners until the word is hovered or focused, keeping their room so nothing reflows; the word is then focusable with a dotted underline that thickens on hover and the ink focus ring. CSS only, no JavaScript.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/ruby`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `base`: `ReactNode` — The characters (group ruby).
  - `reading`: `ReactNode` — The reading over the whole base.
  - `parts`: `[base, reading?][]` — One reading per character or group (mono ruby). Takes over base and reading.
  - `position`: `"over" | "under"` (default `"over"`) — Side of the reading. In vertical text, over is on the right.
  - `reveal`: `"always" | "hover" | "never"` (default `"always"`) — hover: readings show on hover or focus (room kept). never: hidden but still read aloud.
  - `lang`: `string` (default `"ja"`) — Language of the text.

```tsx
import { Ruby } from "@/components/manga/ruby"

<p lang="ja">
  <Ruby parts={[["漢", "かん"], ["字", "じ"]]} />を<Ruby base="読" reading="よ" />む
</p>
```

### Vertical Text (`vertical-text`)

Vertical writing (tategaki) with CSS writing modes: characters run top to bottom and columns right to left, whatever the page's reading order or writing direction, and the text stays real text. A column height wraps it into new columns; the reading, lettering or SFX face; Latin letters lying on their side or upright; an optional fine rule between columns like a manuscript sheet. Tcy sets a short number upright in one cell (tate-chu-yoko).

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/vertical-text`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `as`: `"div" | "p" | "span" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4"` (default `"div"`) — Rendered element.
  - `height`: `string` — Column height (any CSS length). Text wraps into a new column on the left.
  - `font`: `"reading" | "letter" | "sfx"` (default `"reading"`) — Reading face, lettering face or the SFX face.
  - `upright`: `boolean` (default `false`) — Latin letters stand upright instead of lying on their side.
  - `ruled`: `boolean` (default `false`) — A fine ink rule between columns.
  - `lang`: `string` (default `"ja"`) — Language of the text.

```tsx
import { Tcy, VerticalText } from "@/components/manga/vertical-text"

<VerticalText height="12rem">
  雨の夜、<Tcy>12</Tcy>時。
</VerticalText>
```

### Bilingual Bubble (`bilingual-bubble`)

A SpeechBubble (wrapped, not changed) that switches between the original line and its translation. Both texts share one grid cell, so the bubble keeps the size of the longer one and never jumps; the hidden one is invisible and aria-hidden, each carries its own lang. A two-cell switch sits on top of the bubble (pressed buttons: the current language an ink flat that sweeps in, cells thicken on hover, a click hits, focus stays inside the cell, 44px on phones); the line that comes in pops in steps. Controlled or not; every SpeechBubble variant and tail.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/bilingual-bubble`
- Categories: manga
- Props:
  - `original`: `ReactNode` — The line as first written.
  - `translation`: `ReactNode` — The same line, translated.
  - `originalLang / translationLang`: `string` (default `"ja" / "en"`) — Language of each text.
  - `originalLabel / translationLabel`: `string` (default `"JA" / "EN"`) — Labels on the switch.
  - `showing`: `"original" | "translation"` — Shown text (controlled).
  - `defaultShowing`: `"original" | "translation"` (default `"original"`) — Shown text at first.
  - `onShowingChange`: `(showing) => void` — Called when the switch changes.
  - `switchAlign`: `"start" | "end"` (default `"end"`) — Where the switch sits above the bubble.
  - `switchLabel`: `string` (default `"Language"`) — Spoken name of the switch.

```tsx
import { BilingualBubble } from "@/components/manga/bilingual-bubble"

<BilingualBubble original="おはよう！" translation="Good morning!" tail="bottom" />
```

### Manga Reader (`manga-reader`)

A webtoon-style chapter reader made only with mangacn: a top bar with the series and chapter, a Full screen toggle (pressed button) and a Chapters button opening a Sheet headed by a VolumeCard of the current volume (the cover you pass, ongoing status, chapters read / out as a running-line bar) above the chapter list (the current chapter is an ink flat, read chapters carry a brush check), a reading-order switch of pressed buttons (Manga RTL / Western LTR) that sets data-reading on the root and flips the previous / next chapter buttons, a ReadingProgress bar with a "Page 3 / 9" counter fed by the strip, a ReaderStrip of the chapter's pages (lazy images, END panel), previous / next chapter buttons and a comments strip (Message, Bubble, ReactionPicker, Input). From @md/main up, on screens at least 36rem tall, the reader fills a 46rem frame that scrolls inside and the progress bar sticks to the top of the frame and measures it; on phones it follows the page and the progress bar sticks to the bottom edge. Full screen makes the reader root fixed inset-0 with its own scroll (data-fullscreen="immersive", also the fallback when the Fullscreen API is missing or refused, e.g. iOS Safari) and asks the browser for full screen on the document element (data-fullscreen="native"), so the Sheet still opens above it; Escape or the button leaves. Works in light, dark, any accent and at phone width.

import { MangaReader } from "@/components/manga/blocks/manga-reader"

### Sign in (`sign-in`)

The sign-in screen of the mangacn auth flow, made only with the kit. A manga Panel: the picture you pass for each state (pictures), focus SpeedLines around her, a SpeechBubble ('Welcome back! Your shelf missed you.', a shout bubble 'Huh?!' on error, 'Yes!' on success), a Manpu mark and the Sfx ドキッ. The form, in a case (G1) when there is room: email Field, password with a show/hide toggle inside an InputGroup (aria-pressed, touch-hit), a 'Keep me signed in' Checkbox, a Sign in Button with its loading state (fields stay enabled), a 'Forgot password?' link, SocialButtons (Google, Apple by default, no logo shipped) behind an AuthDivider 'or', and 'New here? Create an account'. Errors: field errors (Field) with focus on the first wrong field; wrong credentials (demo: the password 'wrongpass') show a jagged accent box with a '!' mark that shakes, role=alert (G8). Success: an accent Stamp and an 'Enter your code' button for the second step. Links call onNavigate and never navigate. One column on phones with 44px touch targets; container queries widen it. Works in light, dark, any accent and with Radix or Base UI.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/sign-in`
- Categories: blocks
- Props:
  - `pictures`: `{ idle?: string; error?: string; done?: string }` — Image URLs for the panel, one per state. Without them the panel shows its speed lines only.
  - `className`: `string` — Size and placement of the whole interface.
  - `onNavigate`: `(screen: "sign-in" | "sign-up" | "forgot-password" | "verify-code" | "reset-password") => void` (default `undefined`) — Called by 'Forgot password?', 'Create an account' and 'Enter your code'. Without it these do nothing.
  - `providers`: `{ id: string; label: string; logo?: React.ReactNode }[]` (default `[{ id: "google", label: "Continue with Google" }, { id: "apple", label: "Continue with Apple" }]`) — Third-party sign-in buttons. The block ships no logo; an empty list hides the divider and the buttons.
  - `titleAs`: `"h1" | "h2"` (default `"h1"`) — The title's heading level: "h1" when the block is the page, "h2" inside a page that already has its h1.

```tsx
import { SignIn } from "@/components/manga/blocks/sign-in"

<SignIn
  className="min-h-svh"
  onNavigate={(screen) => router.push(`/${screen}`)}
  providers={[{ id: "google", label: "Continue with Google", logo: <GoogleMark /> }]}
/>
```

### Verify code (`verify-code`)

The one-time code screen of a manga auth flow, made only with mangacn. A manga Panel shows the picture you pass for each state (pictures), focus SpeedLines around her, 'ピコン' Sfx lettering and a SpeechBubble that reacts: 'Check your inbox!', a shout bubble 'Huh?!' on error, 'Yes!' on success. From 48rem of container width the panel sits on the start side at the full height of the form; under it the panel is a 4:3 picture above the form. The form, in a case (G1) when there is room: InputOTP with one group of 6 digits (fits 360px), a Button with its loading state, a resend link after a 30 s countdown (only the end and the resend are announced) and 'Use another email'. Fewer than six digits shows a Field error; the wrong code 000000 shows the G8 error box (accent fill, edge-jagged, '!' mark, shake, role=alert) and the InputOTP invalid look, focus back in the code; any other full code loads, then the success Stamp lands with the next action. The purpose prop (sign-in, sign-up, reset) changes the copy, the stamp ('Welcome back!', 'Welcome!', 'Verified!') and the next screen. Links call onNavigate and never navigate by themselves. One column on phones with 44px touch targets; container queries widen it. Works in light, dark, any accent and with Radix or Base UI.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/verify-code`
- Categories: blocks
- Props:
  - `pictures`: `{ idle?: string; error?: string; done?: string }` — Image URLs for the panel, one per state. Without them the panel shows its speed lines only.
  - `purpose`: `"sign-in" | "sign-up" | "reset"` (default `"sign-in"`) — What the code confirms: changes the copy, the stamp and the next step (reset goes on to reset-password).
  - `email`: `string` (default `"mika@inkwell.app"`) — The address the code was sent to.
  - `onNavigate`: `(screen: "sign-in" | "sign-up" | "forgot-password" | "verify-code" | "reset-password") => void` — Called by 'Use another email' (back to sign-in, sign-up or forgot-password) and, for reset, by 'Choose a new password'. Without it they do nothing.
  - `onContinue`: `() => void` — Called by the button shown once a sign-in or sign-up code is accepted.
  - `className`: `string` — Size and placement of the whole interface.
  - `titleAs`: `"h1" | "h2"` (default `"h1"`) — The title's heading level: "h1" when the block is the page, "h2" inside a page that already has its h1.

```tsx
import { VerifyCode } from "@/components/manga/blocks/verify-code"

<VerifyCode purpose="sign-in" email="mika@inkwell.app" onNavigate={(screen) => router.push(`/${screen}`)} />
```

### Reset password (`reset-password`)

The last screen of a manga 'forgot password' flow, made only with mangacn. A manga Panel shows the picture you pass for each state (pictures), focus SpeedLines around her, 'キラッ' Sfx lettering and a SpeechBubble that reacts: 'A fresh start.', a shout bubble 'Huh?!' on error, 'Yes!' on success. From 48rem of container width the panel sits on the start side at the full height of the form; under it the panel is a 4:3 picture above the form. The form, in a case (G1) when there is room: a new password in an InputGroup with a show/hide toggle (aria-pressed, 'Show password' / 'Hide password', touch-hit, it reveals both fields) and a PasswordStrength gauge, a confirmation Input, a Save Button with its loading state. Field errors (empty, weak when the score is under 2, mismatch) appear on submit with focus on the first wrong field; the demo 'server' refuses the current password 'Lanterns42!' with the G8 error box (accent fill, edge-jagged, '!' mark, shake, role=alert). Success: the 'Saved!' Stamp lands and 'Back to sign in' calls onNavigate. One column on phones with 44px touch targets; container queries widen it. Works in light, dark, any accent and with Radix or Base UI.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/reset-password`
- Categories: blocks
- Props:
  - `pictures`: `{ idle?: string; error?: string; done?: string }` — Image URLs for the panel, one per state. Without them the panel shows its speed lines only.
  - `email`: `string` (default `"mika@inkwell.app"`) — The account whose password changes.
  - `onNavigate`: `(screen: "sign-in" | "sign-up" | "forgot-password" | "verify-code" | "reset-password") => void` — Called by 'Back to sign in' after the password is saved. Without it the button does nothing.
  - `className`: `string` — Size and placement of the whole interface.
  - `titleAs`: `"h1" | "h2"` (default `"h1"`) — The title's heading level: "h1" when the block is the page, "h2" inside a page that already has its h1.

```tsx
import { ResetPassword } from "@/components/manga/blocks/reset-password"

<ResetPassword email="mika@inkwell.app" onNavigate={(screen) => router.push(`/${screen}`)} />
```

### Sign up (`sign-up`)

The sign-up screen of the mangacn auth flow, made only with the kit. A manga Panel: the picture you pass for each state (pictures), focus SpeedLines, a SpeechBubble ('A new reader!', a shout bubble 'Huh?!' on error, 'Yes!' on success), a Manpu sparkle and the Sfx ワクワク. From 48rem of container width the panel stands full height on the start side of the form; narrower, it sits above the form in 4:3 with the character whole. The form, in a case (G1) when there is room: name and email Fields, password with a show/hide toggle inside an InputGroup (aria-pressed, touch-hit) and a PasswordStrength gauge, a terms Checkbox ('I accept the Terms and the Privacy notice'), a Create account Button with its loading state (fields stay enabled), SocialButtons (Google, Apple by default, no logo shipped) behind an AuthDivider 'or', and 'Already have an account? Sign in'. Errors with focus on the first wrong field: empty fields, invalid email, weak password (passwordScore under 2), terms unchecked; a taken email (demo: an address starting with 'taken') shows a jagged accent box with a '!' mark that shakes, role=alert (G8). Success: an accent Stamp 'Created!', 'Check your inbox' and an 'Enter the code' button. Links call onNavigate and never navigate. One column on phones with 44px touch targets; container queries widen it. Works in light, dark, any accent and with Radix or Base UI.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/sign-up`
- Categories: blocks
- Props:
  - `pictures`: `{ idle?: string; error?: string; done?: string }` — Image URLs for the panel, one per state. Without them the panel shows its speed lines only.
  - `className`: `string` — Size and placement of the whole interface.
  - `onNavigate`: `(screen: "sign-in" | "sign-up" | "forgot-password" | "verify-code" | "reset-password") => void` (default `undefined`) — Called by 'Sign in' and 'Enter the code'. Without it these do nothing.
  - `providers`: `{ id: string; label: string; logo?: React.ReactNode }[]` (default `[{ id: "google", label: "Continue with Google" }, { id: "apple", label: "Continue with Apple" }]`) — Third-party sign-up buttons. The block ships no logo; an empty list hides the divider and the buttons.
  - `titleAs`: `"h1" | "h2"` (default `"h1"`) — The title's heading level: "h1" when the block is the page, "h2" inside a page that already has its h1.

```tsx
import { SignUp } from "@/components/manga/blocks/sign-up"

<SignUp
  className="min-h-svh"
  onNavigate={(screen) => router.push(`/${screen}`)}
  providers={[{ id: "google", label: "Continue with Google", logo: <GoogleMark /> }]}
/>
```

### Forgot password (`forgot-password`)

The password-recovery screen of the mangacn auth flow, made only with the kit. A manga Panel: the picture you pass for each state (pictures), focus SpeedLines, a SpeechBubble ('Forgot it? It happens.', a shout bubble 'Huh?!' on error, 'Yes!' on success), a Manpu sweat drop and the Sfx ハッ. From 48rem of container width the panel stands full height on the start side of the form; narrower, it sits above the form in 4:3 with the character whole. The form, in a case (G1) when there is room: an email Field, a Send code Button with its loading state (the field stays enabled) and a 'Back to sign in' link. Errors with focus on the field: empty or invalid email; an unknown email (demo: an address containing 'unknown') shows a jagged accent box with a '!' mark that shakes, role=alert (G8). Success: an accent Stamp 'Sent!' and an 'Enter the code' button. Links call onNavigate and never navigate. One column on phones with 44px touch targets; container queries widen it. Works in light, dark, any accent and with Radix or Base UI.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/forgot-password`
- Categories: blocks
- Props:
  - `pictures`: `{ idle?: string; error?: string; done?: string }` — Image URLs for the panel, one per state. Without them the panel shows its speed lines only.
  - `className`: `string` — Size and placement of the whole interface.
  - `onNavigate`: `(screen: "sign-in" | "sign-up" | "forgot-password" | "verify-code" | "reset-password") => void` (default `undefined`) — Called by 'Back to sign in' and 'Enter the code'. Without it these do nothing.
  - `titleAs`: `"h1" | "h2"` (default `"h1"`) — The title's heading level: "h1" when the block is the page, "h2" inside a page that already has its h1.

```tsx
import { ForgotPassword } from "@/components/manga/blocks/forgot-password"

<ForgotPassword className="min-h-svh" onNavigate={(screen) => router.push(`/${screen}`)} />
```

### Story landing (`story-landing`)

A product landing page told as a short manga, made only with mangacn, for an invented habit app: a top bar, an opening MagazineCover (masthead band, issue box, cover lines around the picture you pass) beside a lettering headline, a shout Button and a contents page that lists the chapters like the first page of a volume; then four sections titled with ChapterTitle (big number, vertical text): a Yonkoma strip on the page model that explains the product in four beats (a column on phones, four in a row from 40rem; captions and an Sfx put on the panels with Place), a guide character who talks the reader through it in a DialogueBox, reader quotes in SpeechBubbles, and a closing call to action. Jumping to a chapter plays a stepped SceneTransition (four ink panels, a "Meanwhile…" caption), then focus moves to the section; starting plays an ink wipe and reveals a finished state with an Sfx. Reduced motion: instant. Container queries widen it; links never navigate; nothing is posted. Works in light, dark, any accent, both reading orders and at phone width.

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add Romcharted/mangacn/story-landing`
- Categories: blocks
- Props:
  - `art`: `{ cover?: string; guide?: string; reader?: string; beats?: [string, string, string, string] }` — The cover, the faces and the strip pictures (image URLs). Without them the cover is screentone and the panels stay blank.
  - `className`: `string` — Size and placement of the whole interface.
  - `titleAs`: `"h1" | "h2"` (default `"h1"`) — The title's heading level: "h1" when the block is the page, "h2" inside a page that already has its h1.

```tsx
import { StoryLanding } from "@/components/manga/blocks/story-landing"

<StoryLanding />
```
